name: Choquequirao trek
why: Machu Picchu's 'sister' with almost nobody there: four days down and up the Apurímac canyon to Inca terraces decorated with white llamas.
book: Entry ticket at the site. Mules and muleteers from Cachora.
water: Camps have water; buy at the campsites.
dangers: 1,500 m down to the river and 1,500 m up the other side, in the heat: the hardest day of any Peru trek.
No shade at midday in the canyon.

points.name: Cachora
points.note: The village at 2,900 m where muleteers wait; a dirt road (taxi possible) leads on to Capuliyoc.

points.name: Capuliyoc viewpoint over the Apurímac canyon
points.note: The canyon opens 1,500 m below; Choquequirao is on the far slope. From here it is all downhill to the river.

points.name: Playa Rosalina on the Apurímac river
points.note: The camp and bridge at the bottom, about 1,500 m: camp here, then climb 1,600 m in the early cool.

points.name: Choquequirao
points.note: About 3,050 m: the plaza, the terraces and the white llamas in stone. Camp by the site and see it the next day.
